brief.headline: Push for a 2.4-point margin rollback — they earn 7.4% net vs 5.0% peer median and carry an A+ rating, so they have room to share the spread.

priceAsk.summary: Request a price reduction that brings their margin closer to the Glass Works peer median of 5.0%
priceAsk.target: A reduction reflecting the 2.4-point margin premium they enjoy (7.4% net margin vs 5.0% peer median)
priceAsk.basis: PGP earns 7.4% net margin against a 5.0% peer median — 240 basis points above the pack. Their A+ rating and ₹2899.48 Cr free cash flow show they can absorb a trim without stress.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days earlier in exchange for a price discount equal to their borrowing cost of 7.02%
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Moving to 15-day terms would lock ₹1.64 L of our working capital (workingCapitalFreedIf15DayMore)

brief.financialLeverage: PGP is investment-grade (CARE A+ / Stable) with a 7.4% net margin — 240 basis points fatter than the 5.0% peer median — and ₹2899.48 Cr in free cash flow. Debt-to-equity of 0.70x and interest coverage of 2.84x are comfortable. We're only 0.01% of their ₹3373.51 Cr revenue, so our direct volume leverage is negligible. However, the margin premium and solid balance sheet mean they can afford to give ground on price without endangering supply. The grey-zone Altman Z of 1.45, EPF payment delays, and pending legal cases warrant a firm but not aggressive stance — focus on commercial logic (margin gap, alternate competition) rather than a squeeze that might spook a supplier already showing operational strain.

evidence.point: PGP's net margin is 240 basis points above the Glass Works peer median
Investment-grade credit rating indicates low continuity risk
Strong free cash generation gives pricing flexibility
We represent a tiny share of their business, limiting our standalone leverage
Their borrowing cost makes early payment valuable to them
HDPE resin import benchmark provides a material-cost reference

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter at ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, already qualified as a second source for packaging, with a B health score (65/100) — a robust, scalable alternate for pharma bottles and caps

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, B health score 73/100) specialising in pails, containers, and pharma packaging — a credible second source for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed player with ₹701.17 Cr revenue and broad moulded/blow-moulded capability across bottles and caps, offering competition despite a C health score (51/100)

risks: Altman Z of 1.45 puts PGP in the grey zone — push too hard and we risk tipping a financially stretched supplier into deeper distress
EPF payment delays and pending legal cases signal operational or cash-flow strain; validate continuity and quality before locking in higher volumes
At 0.01% of their revenue we have almost no standalone clout — this negotiation hinges on credible alternate competition and the margin-gap logic, not volume threat
Their 29-day payable cycle vs 42-day peer median suggests they already squeeze their own suppliers; limited room to pass further cost pressure upstream
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to discuss how your 7.4% net margin — well above the 5.0% Glass Works median — can translate into a more competitive price for us, especially given the strong alternates we're now qualifying.
